headline: Nvidia's beat-and-raise ($115.8B revenue, ≈$130B Q4 guide) has Nasdaq futures up ≈1% after a five-month-low S&P close. Rates and metals tell a harder story: gold is at a one-year low under $3,800, copper is at a five-month low, and the long end faces a $16B new 20Y at noon CT and the October FOMC minutes at 1 PM CT.
summary: Tuesday's AP closes: S&P 500 7,340.53 (−1.0%, a five-month low and its 4th straight loss), Dow 50,759.42 (−848.75, −1.6%), Nasdaq Composite 24,328.38 (−0.7%), Russell 2000 2,701.87 (−1.5%). Breadth was ugly, with only 75 S&P names up and all 11 sectors down. This morning, S&P futures are ≈+0.3–0.5%, Nasdaq 100 futures ≈+0.9–1.1% and Dow futures ≈+0.2–0.3% (Bloomberg, TipRanks).

Nvidia FQ3 FY27 (8-K): revenue $115.8B (+103% y/y) vs the $108B ±2% guide and ≈$109B consensus; data center $107.6B; non-GAAP GM 74.9%; non-GAAP EPS $2.68 vs ≈$2.48 (LSEG). The Q4 guide is ≈$130B ±3% vs ≈$125.3B consensus, but GM guidance steps down to ≈71–72%, it includes an extra week, and it assumes zero China data-center revenue. Shares were $162.94 (+4.8%) at 7:59 PM ET from a $155.46 close. Board chair Harvey Jones ruled out reinstating Huang, and the WSJ reports an SEC civil inquiry into Nvidia's disclosures around his exit.

Rates: the 10Y is ≈5.09% and the 30Y ≈5.44% early (≈−1–2bp), the 2Y ≈4.80%, and 2s10s ≈+29bp. Fed funds is 3.75–4.00%, with a December 8–9 +25bp hike ≈96–99% priced. Today's long-end tests are the new $16B 20Y (Nov 2046) at 12:00 PM CT and the Oct 27–28 minutes (10–2 hold; Cook and Hammack dissented for a hike) at 1:00 PM CT. The October 20Y reopening cleared near 5.47%.

Metals are breaking down on the Fed, not geopolitics. Spot gold fell ≈1.4% to $3,796 by 0242 GMT and later traded ≈$3,770, the lowest since September 2025, and Goldman cut its end-2026 target to $4,150 from $4,650. Silver is ≈$45.7, platinum ≈$1,377 and palladium ≈$954 (Fortune, 6:30 AM ET). LME copper fell as much as 1.6% to $13,019/t (lowest since June 24), ≈11% below the $14,617 record. DXY is ≈103.8, near a 19-month high, with USD/JPY ≈159.3.

Consumer earnings were strong, but much of it came from tariff refunds. Target comps were +5.6% (vs ≈+3.6% est.) with EPS $2.65 vs ≈$2.07, including $301M of pretax tariff-refund benefit. Lowe's adj. EPS was $3.10 vs $2.88, but $0.34 of that came from IEEPA tariff refunds; it raised FY sales to ≈$92.5B and held EPS at $12.25. TJX reports before the open (consensus EPS $1.33, revenue $15.81B). October housing starts are at 7:30 AM CT.

Capital markets: Anthropic prices tonight and trades Thursday on Nasdaq as 'ANT'. The order book is reportedly ≈6–7x covered, and the WSJ and CNBC expect pricing above the $70–78 range (possibly >$80). Banking: JPMorgan named CIB CFO Bregje de Best (43) to succeed Jeremy Barnum as CFO after Q1 2027; Barnum becomes Vice Chairman. Ameris agreed to buy Bank of Central Florida (≈$1.2B assets) for ≈$180M in stock.

calendar.consensus: TGT EPS ≈$2.07, comps ≈+3.6%; LOW adj EPS $2.88
calendar.why: Both beat, but tariff refunds inflated the beats ($301M pretax at TGT, $0.34/sh at LOW). Underlying consumer strength is less than the headlines suggest, which matters for how hot the Fed thinks demand is.
An off-price read on middle-income shoppers. Watch Marmaxx comps and freight/fuel margin pressure.
Builder sentiment is at a 14-year low with the 10Y above 5%. A weak print backs the view that hikes are already biting the rate-sensitive economy.
WTI is at ≈3-month lows on glut talk despite Hormuz attacks. A big build would feed the lower-breakevens story.
Recent auctions tailed. A tail here would confirm that the long end needs more term premium even with the 10Y at 5.1%.

calendar.event: Fed Gov. Barr (NY Fed community development event); FinRegLab AI panel ≈1:00 PM
calendar.why: Supervision and community banking, a commercial-banking angle more than a policy one.
How many participants leaned toward hiking, and whether anyone discussed 50bp, decides whether the 2Y can rise further from ≈4.80%.

calendar.prior: Tue: one more hike likely, nothing 'dramatic'
calendar.why: His second appearance in two days. Any shift after the minutes moves the SOFR strip.
A barometer of the hawkish wing's appetite for a 2027 hike path.

calendar.why: Payments topic, but any Q&A on December sizing matters.

calendar.event: Anthropic IPO pricing; trades Thu on Nasdaq (ANT)
calendar.why: One of the largest IPOs ever and a test of risk appetite and ECM capacity. Funding the allocation may have pressured software stocks Tuesday.
Real yields are ≈2.87%, near 18-year highs, and this is the key input for gold.

rates.title: Long end gets a small reprieve before a big supply test
rates.body: The 10Y is ≈5.09% and the 30Y ≈5.44% early Wednesday, ≈1–2bp richer, after Tuesday's risk-off slide ended near 5.11%. The new $16B 20Y prices at noon CT. The October 20Y reopening cleared near 5.47%, and recent coupon auctions have tailed.
rates.simple: A Treasury yield is the interest the government pays to borrow, and it moves opposite to bond prices. Today the Treasury sells $16 billion of brand-new 20-year bonds, and if buyers are lukewarm it has to offer a higher rate (a 'tail'). That would push up long-term borrowing costs like mortgages.

rates.title: Minutes are the 2Y's catalyst; December is priced, 2027 is the trade
rates.body: December +25bp is ≈96–99% priced (FedWatch / futures trackers), Kalshi has ≈8.5% for 50bp, and one estimate has Dec-27 SOFR futures implying ≈4.78%, about three more hikes. The October meeting held 10–2 with two hike dissents, and Waller has floated 50bp if core runs hot.
rates.simple: The Fed sets a short-term interest rate, and markets are almost certain it will raise it in December. What's still undecided is how many more hikes follow in 2027. Today's minutes (the notes from the last meeting) show how many officials wanted to move sooner, which shifts bets on that path.
rates.source: MPA Mag / Prediction Markets Picks / Admiral Markets

rates.title: Global yields: UK CPI ticks up, Bunds near 1-month highs, JGB auction soft
rates.body: UK October CPI rose to 3.6% (from 3.5%) with core steady at 2.8% and services 3.7% (below 3.8% est.). BoE December hike odds were trimmed to ≈80% and GBP fell 0.4% to $1.314. The Bund 10Y is ≈3.35–3.37% on ECB hike bets. Japan's 20Y JGB auction bid-to-cover fell to 3.64 from 5.84.
rates.simple: Other big economies are also fighting inflation with higher rates. When foreign bonds pay more, fewer investors need to buy US Treasuries, so US rates have to stay high to attract buyers. Japan's weak bond sale is a warning that one of America's biggest lenders is finding better deals at home.
rates.source: Trading & Investment News / Trading Economics / Bloomberg

derivatives.title: Nvidia's ≈±8% implied move delivered ≈+5%; vol curve was inverted
derivatives.body: Options priced ≈7.7–8% into the print, and the stock was +4.8% after hours, so straddle buyers likely lost money. Saxo notes Nvidia reported into an inverted volatility curve (near-dated vol above longer-dated). VIX was ≈25 Tuesday and should compress if the futures bid holds.
derivatives.simple: Options are contracts that pay off when a stock moves a lot, and their price shows how big a move traders expect. Traders expected about an 8% swing and got about 5%, so people who paid up for protection lost money. When near-term options cost more than long-term ones, the market is nervous about the next few days specifically.

derivatives.title: Rates vol still elevated: MOVE ≈101
derivatives.body: The MOVE index is ≈101–102 (≈91st percentile of the past year, vs ≈55 early in 2026 and >113 in early October). Term premium fell ≈19bp over the past month even as hike expectations rose, so real yields, not inflation fear, are carrying the 5% 10Y.
derivatives.simple: MOVE measures how much traders expect Treasury yields to swing, like a VIX for bonds. At about 101 it's high, which makes hedging more expensive for banks, mortgage lenders and pension funds. The rise in yields is coming from a higher inflation-adjusted rate rather than from fear of inflation itself.
derivatives.source: Le Private Banker / The Weekend Spread

derivatives.title: CME: record October, Treasury complex the standout
derivatives.body: CME's October ADV was a record 30M contracts (+15% y/y). Treasury futures and options ADV rose 48% to 9.2M, SOFR futures and options rose 5% to 4.9M, and rates overall averaged 14.78M/day, the most active October ever. Eris SOFR swap futures OI hit a record ≈900K on Nov 2.
derivatives.simple: CME is the Chicago exchange where investors trade contracts that bet on or hedge future interest rates. Trading is surging because rates are moving so much that everyone needs protection. That is good business for CME and a sign of how jittery bond markets are.

metals.title: Gold under $3,800: one-year low as 5% yields win
metals.body: Spot gold fell ≈1.4% to $3,796 by 0242 GMT and traded ≈$3,770 later, the lowest since September 2025, despite the Iran conflict. Goldman cut its end-2026 target to $4,150 from $4,650 because a hawkish Fed blocks the usual support from falling yields. 10Y TIPS ≈2.87% raises the cost of holding gold.
metals.simple: Gold pays no interest, so when safe government bonds pay over 5% (nearly 2.9% after inflation), holding gold costs more. A strong dollar also makes gold pricier for foreign buyers. That's why gold is falling even with a war in the Middle East that would normally lift it.

metals.title: Silver and PGMs follow gold lower
metals.body: Silver was $45.74 at 6:30 AM ET, ≈−3% from Tuesday's ≈$47 area. Platinum is $1,377 and palladium $954. Silver's higher beta to both real yields and industrial demand makes it underperform gold on down days.
metals.simple: Silver is partly a precious metal and partly an industrial input (solar panels, electronics), so it swings harder than gold. It gets hit twice when rates rise and the economy looks wobbly. Platinum and palladium, used in car exhaust systems, are being dragged down too.

metals.title: Copper at 5-month low: AI wobble plus China gloom
metals.body: LME 3M copper fell as much as 1.6% to $13,019/t, the lowest since June 24 and ≈10.9% below the $14,617 record of Sept 8, and traded ≈$13,078 midday. SHFE was −1.5% at 99,840 yuan. The drivers are a stronger dollar, AI-sector upheaval (data-center wiring demand) and a weak China outlook.
metals.simple: Copper goes into wiring, power grids and AI data centers, so its price is a quick read on industrial demand. It's falling because investors worry that both AI spending and China's economy are cooling, and because a strong dollar makes it costlier abroad. Nvidia's strong results could steady it if the AI fear eases.

banking.title: JPMorgan sets CFO succession: de Best to replace Barnum
banking.body: JPM named Bregje de Best (43), CFO of the Commercial & Investment Bank since June 2025 and formerly co-head of Global Corporate Banking, to succeed Jeremy Barnum after the Q1 2027 report. Barnum becomes Vice Chairman and will handle January/April earnings and the February Investor Day.
banking.simple: The CFO runs a company's finances and explains results to investors. JPMorgan, the largest US bank, is promoting someone from its corporate and investment bank, which is a sign of where its leadership bench is. An orderly handover avoids rattling shareholders.

banking.title: Anthropic IPO: pricing tonight, above range expected
banking.body: 825M shares were marketed at $70–78. CNBC and WSJ sources expect pricing above the range (possibly >$80), with the book ≈6–7x covered and several orders over $10B. At the top of the range, the IPO plus a $26B private placement raises ≈$90B at a ≈$1.4T valuation. Sustainalytics rated it 'high ESG risk'.
banking.simple: An IPO is when a private company first sells shares to the public, and banks earn fees for running it. Demand at six to seven times the shares on offer lets Anthropic charge more. A deal this size shows investors still have a big appetite for AI, and it pulls cash out of other stocks.

banking.title: Ameris buys Bank of Central Florida for ≈$180M in stock
banking.body: All-stock deal at 0.6279 ABCB shares per share (≈$51.80 implied on the Nov 12 close of $82.50) for a Lakeland/Tampa lender with ≈$1.2B assets and $1.1B deposits. It needs target-shareholder and regulatory approval. Separately, the Richmond Fed approved John Marshall's merger with Bank of Clarke; shareholder votes are Nov 19.
banking.simple: Regional banks are buying smaller local banks to gain deposits (cheap funding) and customers in growing markets like Florida. Paying in stock instead of cash preserves capital. Steady small deals and regulatory approvals show bank consolidation is still moving.

banking.title: Northern Trust at a 52-week low
banking.body: NTRS hit a 52-week low Tuesday and crossed below its 50-day moving average. Investing.com cites a ≈6.8% dividend yield. Custody banks are being squeezed by risk-off asset values and a curve where deposit costs rise with hikes.
banking.simple: Northern Trust is a Chicago bank that holds and manages assets for wealthy people and institutions, so its fees rise and fall with markets. Falling stock and bond prices cut those fees. A high dividend yield means the stock price has dropped a lot relative to its payout.

cnbc.title: Nvidia takes a step forward with stronger outlook
cnbc.body: Revenue was $115.8B vs a $108B guide and the Q4 guide is ≈$130B vs ≈$125B expected, but the GM guide eases to ≈71–72% and the quarter includes an extra week. CNBC also reported the board isn't considering bringing back Huang.
cnbc.simple: Nvidia makes the chips that power AI, so its results are a scorecard for the whole AI boom. It sold far more than promised and expects even more next quarter, which calms fears the boom is fading. Its profit margin per chip is slipping a bit, though.

cnbc.title: Gold slides to over one-year low
cnbc.body: Spot gold was −1.4% at $3,796 early, the lowest since Sept 2025, on a firm dollar and ≈96.7% odds of a December hike.
cnbc.simple: Gold is losing out to bonds that now pay well and to a strong dollar. When the Fed raises rates, the opportunity cost of holding gold rises.

cnbc.title: Anthropic likely to price above $70–78 range
cnbc.body: Sources told CNBC the IPO will likely price above range Wednesday, ahead of Thursday's Nasdaq debut.
cnbc.simple: Strong demand lets a company sell its shares at a higher price than first planned. For the banks running the deal, that means bigger fees and a showcase win.

cnbc.title: Treasury yields steady after retail sales
cnbc.body: The 10Y slipped ≈1bp to ≈5.109% Tuesday as stocks sold off, and FedWatch shows ≈95% odds of a December hike.
cnbc.simple: Bonds barely rallied on a bad stock day, which means they are not acting as their usual safety cushion. That's because the Fed is still raising rates.

wsj.title: SEC opens civil inquiry into Nvidia disclosures around Huang's exit
wsj.body: The WSJ reports the SEC is examining whether Nvidia's disclosures misled investors after Huang's departure, and the board chair said he isn't considering bringing him back.
wsj.simple: The SEC is the regulator that makes sure public companies tell investors the truth. A 'civil inquiry' is an early-stage look, not charges, but it adds legal risk to the world's most important AI company.

wsj.title: Anthropic expects to price above $80
wsj.body: The WSJ reports Anthropic now expects pricing above the previously marketed $70–78 range on strong demand.
wsj.simple: When investors line up to buy, the company raises its price. That brings in more money for the company and resets valuations for other AI firms.

wsj.title: JPMorgan picks de Best as next CFO
wsj.body: The WSJ covers JPMorgan's CFO succession: Barnum to Vice Chairman, with CIB CFO Bregje de Best taking over after Q1 2027.
wsj.simple: The biggest US bank is lining up its next finance chief. It's an orderly handoff that keeps investors calm.

wsj.title: White House pulls FDA nominee Overton
wsj.body: The nomination of Dr. Heidi Overton to lead the FDA was withdrawn amid doubts about Senate confirmation.
wsj.simple: The FDA approves drugs and medical devices, so a leadership vacuum can slow decisions that pharma and biotech stocks depend on.

tribune.title: Chicago CFO quits after three months; aldermen seek outside audit
tribune.body: CFO Ashlee Gabrysch resigned Nov 13, the third CFO exit in about a year, reportedly over how the city presents its finances. Aldermen want an IG review and an outside audit, a $500M sewer bond was pulled from the agenda, and Fitch already has Chicago at BBB+ with a negative outlook.
tribune.simple: Chicago borrows by selling municipal bonds, and its credit rating sets how much interest it pays. Losing a third finance chief in a year, during a budget fight, makes rating agencies and bond buyers more nervous. That can raise the city's borrowing costs and, eventually, taxes.

tribune.title: CME: record October volume, rates boom
tribune.body: Chicago-based CME posted record October ADV of 30M contracts, with Treasury futures and options +48% and rates averaging 14.78M/day.
tribune.simple: Volatile interest rates are good for CME because everyone needs to hedge. For a Chicago derivatives career, this is the busiest rates market in years.

tribune.title: Northern Trust slides to 52-week low
tribune.body: The Chicago custody bank hit a 52-week low Tuesday and broke below its 50-day average.
tribune.simple: When markets fall, banks that earn fees on assets they hold for clients earn less. Investors are pricing in that squeeze.

nyt.title: Trump urged Huang to keep fighting for his job before resigning
nyt.body: Per the NYT, Trump called Huang days before his resignation and urged him to fight. The story adds political overlay to the Nvidia governance saga and the SEC inquiry.
nyt.simple: Nvidia's leadership change has become a political story as well as a business one. That raises the odds of more scrutiny from Washington.

nyt.title: Waymo pulls cars off highways after California freeway ban
nyt.body: Waymo temporarily withdrew driverless vehicles from US limited-access highways after California barred it from freeways.
nyt.simple: Self-driving cars need regulators' permission. A state ban shows how fast rules can slow a new technology's rollout.

nyt.title: FAA halts router installs after nationwide ground stop
nyt.body: The FAA suspended installing a router type that may have contributed to last week's nationwide flight stoppage, only the third this century.
nyt.simple: A routine equipment upgrade apparently grounded flights nationwide. It shows how fragile critical tech systems can be, the same theme as this week's bank and Apple outages.

talking_points.point: Gold is at a one-year low under $3,800 despite an active Middle East war, because 10Y TIPS are ≈2.87% (near 18-year highs) and DXY is at a 19-month high. The carry cost of a zero-coupon asset now beats the geopolitical bid. Goldman cut its target to $4,150. The trade-relevant question: does gold bottom when the Fed's 2027 path peaks (watch Dec-27 SOFR ≈4.78%), not when headlines escalate?

The 10Y is at 5.1% but term premium has fallen ≈19bp in a month, so real rates are doing the lifting. Today's $16B new 20Y (October reopening ≈5.47%), Thursday's 10Y TIPS reopening and a soft JGB 20Y (bid-to-cover 3.64 vs 5.84) test whether foreign and real-money demand holds. A tail would steepen 2s30s from ≈+64bp.

Anthropic is ≈6–7x covered and could raise ≈$64B+ in the IPO (≈$90B with the private placement) at a ≈$1.4T valuation, a record ECM fee event in a market where the S&P is at five-month lows. Pair it with JPM's CFO pick coming from the CIB: banks' 2027 earnings depend on capital-markets fees offsetting NII pressure as hikes lift deposit costs.

caveats: WSJ and NYT items come via Reuters press digests (Boursorama, rallies.ai); Tribune is paywalled, so Chicago items use the Sun-Times, Bond Buyer and CME. Index levels are Tuesday's AP closes; futures, yields, gold, silver and WTI are early-morning reads from varying sources and times. The 2Y is approximate, housing-starts consensus differs by source,. Brent was ≈$93 at Tuesday's close; no reliable Wednesday print was found. Yahoo, CNBC and other direct page fetches were blocked in this run, so figures come from search summaries.

updates.label: Midday
updates.headline: The 20Y auction cleared without drama and the 2Y round-tripped back to ≈4.78%, but gold extended its slide to ≈$3,742 (−3%) and the Nvidia bounce is fully gone. NVDA is down ≈2% and the Dow ≈1%, while small caps rally into the 1 PM CT minutes.
points: New $16B 20Y (Nov 2046) reportedly stopped at 5.459% with 2.63x bid-to-cover, described as in line with no meaningful tail (single source, Helious; I couldn't confirm WI or tail elsewhere). That compares with October's 5.469% and 2.73x. Indirect bids were 60.2% (avg 63.7%) and directs 26.7% (avg 24.3%). Foreign demand was softer, but the morning's 'tail = more term premium' risk didn't show up.

2Y is ≈4.78%, down ≈0.5bp on the day after spiking to 4.83% on Waller (CNBC). Futures still price a December hike at ≈95–100%, with 50bp odds ≈11–12.5% depending on the source. The front end is treating Waller as a tail risk, not the base case. The minutes at 1 PM CT and Williams at 1:30 PM CT are the next catalysts.

Stocks at 11:50 AM CT (Yahoo): S&P 500 −0.29%, Nasdaq +0.22%, Dow −1.04%, Russell 2000 +1.08% to 2,731. NVDA is ≈−2.1% to −2.4%. The morning's Nvidia-led relief thesis has failed; leadership is rotating into small caps instead of mega-cap tech.

Gold is ≈$3,742 (−3.1%), a fresh one-year low, below the ≈$3,790 seen at the open, as DXY makes another 52-week high. Real yields near 2.9% and the hike debate keep pressuring non-yielding metals. Silver and copper had no reliable midday print, so their tiles show morning reads.

EIA (week to Nov 13): crude +3.4M bbl to 417.8M vs a Reuters poll of ≈+58K. Gasoline +5.2M (exp. +1.6M), distillates +1.6M, Cushing −1.2M. WTI is ≈$84 (≈−2%) and the S&P energy sector ≈−3%, the weakest sector. Anthropic (ANT) still prices tonight; the order book is covered at the $70–78 range, with reports of ≥$80.
updates.simple: The government sold $16 billion of 20-year bonds, and buyers showed up at about the expected price. That calmed fears that investors would demand much higher interest (yield) to lend to Washington for that long. Short-term rates gave back their jump from the Fed governor's 'big hike' comments, but gold kept falling: a stronger dollar and high inflation-adjusted interest rates make a metal that pays no interest less attractive. Stocks are mixed, with Nvidia's great results failing to lift big tech while smaller companies rallied.

updates.label: Post-open
updates.headline: Waller told CNBC a 50bp December hike is 'probably necessary' and the Fed may need to 'shock people'. The 2Y jumped ≈4bp to ≈4.83%, and the Nvidia bounce faded at the open, with the Dow down ≈400 points and NVDA slightly negative.
points: Waller (CNBC, this morning) wants 50bp at Dec 8–9, or 25bp plus an explicit January signal. The 2Y erased an early ≈2.5bp drop and rose to ≈4.83%. FedWatch still shows ≈95% for 25bp, with ≈10% odds for 50bp, so the morning's '96–99% for +25bp' still holds but the tail toward 50bp is fatter. Williams speaks at 1:30 PM CT and has pushed back on 'dramatic action'.

October housing starts came in at 1.309M SAAR (+9.9% m/m vs a revised 1.191M; consensus ≈1.245–1.27M). Single-family starts were 864K, but permits fell ≈7.4% to 1.295M, with single-family permits −8.7% to 772K. The strong starts headline masks a weak forward signal, which tempers the 'hikes are biting housing' read in this morning's calendar.

Open (Reuters): Dow −0.26% at 50,627, S&P 500 +0.21% at 7,355.7, Nasdaq +0.65% at 24,486. Since then CNBC shows the Dow down ≈400 points and NVDA <1% lower, reversing a ≈+4–5% pre-market gain, so the morning thesis of an Nvidia-led relief rally is not holding so far.

TJX Q3 FY27: comps +4% (plan 2–3%), Marmaxx +2%, sales $16.0B (+6%, ≈in line with ≈$16.0B), EPS $1.39 incl. a $0.05 tariff refund (adj. $1.34 vs $1.33 consensus). FY EPS guide raised to $5.33–5.36. It's a third retailer with a tariff-refund boost, after TGT and LOW.

Metals and the dollar are unchanged from the morning: gold ≈$3,790 (−≈1.9%), silver ≈$46 (−≈2.8%), DXY ≈103.7. The new $16B 20Y prices at noon CT, and the minutes come at 1 PM CT. Anthropic still prices tonight (range $70–78; WSJ says possibly >$80).
updates.simple: A Fed governor said on TV that the Fed should raise rates by twice the normal step (half a percentage point) next month to break inflation. That pushed up the 2-year Treasury yield, the interest rate most tied to Fed expectations, and took the shine off Nvidia's strong results. Higher expected rates make borrowing pricier for companies and households, which is why stocks lost their early gains.
